title: Link, Embed, Import, or LTI: Four Ways Into an LMS

zones.label: Link
zones.summary: Students open the resource at its own address.
facts: Students open the resource at its own address.
The resource stays on its own host.
Needs a good link: permanent, direct, and working for the person who receives it.

zones.label: Embed
zones.summary: The resource appears on your course page through a frame.
facts: The resource appears on your course page through a frame.
The page shows it without leaving your course.
Needs a host that allows framing, and no login.

zones.label: Common Cartridge import
zones.summary: A whole unit is copied into the LMS as a package.
facts: A whole unit is copied into the LMS as a package.
A single compressed file with a manifest.
The common exchange form between LMSs. Not every resource offers one.

zones.label: LTI tool
zones.summary: An external tool opens inside the LMS and can send results back.
facts: An external tool opens inside the LMS and can send results back.
It runs on another company's server.
Passes learner information, which raises the privacy questions of Chapter 13.

quiz.question: Which method lets an external quiz tool send each student's score to the LMS gradebook?
quiz.explanation: LTI lets the tool exchange information with the LMS.

quiz.question: Which method makes a simulation appear on your course page through a frame?
quiz.explanation: A frame shows the simulation inside the page.

quiz.question: Which method copies a whole unit, with pages, quizzes, and files, into your course as one package?
quiz.explanation: A package carries the whole unit into the LMS.

quiz.question: Which method just lets students open one reading in a new tab at its own address?
quiz.explanation: A link opens the resource at its own address.
